report: The three sisters have agreed on a shared process, though no price or division is settled. Agreed so far: (1) A will arrange one independent appraisal of the house, accepted by all three; (2) the sisters will read the will together before any price, shares, or sale is discussed — C and A are still exchanging possible times, and B will join whichever works. Positions: A wants to buy the house with her husband, possibly at a discount, but acknowledges she cannot proceed without C's agreement. C will not accept a discounted price and wants a proper valuation first. B needs money from the estate to start a dance studio and is open to A buying at market value so there is cash to split. Next steps: A arranges the appraisal; C sends A some times for the joint will review; after both, the sisters discuss price and shares, with B's studio funding in mind. My role going forward is to keep the agreed sequence visible and check each draft against the shared list of concerns (fair market value, C's consent, B's financial need).
